'''Sunsokua''', officially the '''Republic of Sunsokua''', is a country located in [[East Mahea]]. It primarily comprises the island of [[Hijita]], also known as [[Incolstr]], situated in the [[Haanian Ocean]] between the [[Adrad sea|Adrad]] and [[Praosia sea|Praosia seas]]. Sunsokua lies northwest of [[Ashain]], with [[Pelugrotoa]] also to the northwest, and shares land borders to the south with [[Vayvele]], [[Sadain]], and [[Seiaja]]. The country covers an area of [[List of countries and dependencies by area|737,960 square kilometres (284,928 sq mi)]]. Its geography features central highlands and [[Wikipedia:Coastal_plain|coastal plains]], the latter hosting a major portion of the population. The largest metropolitan area encompasses [[Hikrum]], [[Old Hikrum City]], and [[Tasicudi]]. With a population of approximately [[List of countries and dependencies by population|80 million,]] Sunsokua is one of the most [[List of countries and dependencies by population density|densely populated countries]] in the world.

[[Hijita]] has been inhabited for at least 50,000 years, with the ancestors of the indigenous [[Hijitan peoples]] settling the island around 10,000 years ago. The 4th century saw major [[Kuhn immigration|immigration]] from the [[Earuhty]] and [[Kuhn]] peoples following the [[Yaddan Empire|Yaddan]] invasions of modern-day [[Galca]]. A second wave of settlement occurred in the 9th century during the [[Hoskuran Empire]]'s expansion into the sparsely populated north, continuing under the [[Kingdom of Sunsokua]]. The island experienced a [[The long peace|prolonged period of peace]] beginning in the 11th century, which lasted until the 17th century when the [[Emara|Emaran Empire]] invaded and annexed most of the island by 1640. In the aftermath of the [[Great Imperial War]], [[Hijita]] was given to [[Ashain]] as compensation for its military support. The [[Red War]], led by [[Ho-Aisot Uji]], resulted in a successful [[Sunsokua rebellion|rebellion]] against [[Ashaini occupation of Hijita|Ashaini rule]], and the island ultimately gained independence with the surrender of [[Ashain]]. From the early 1720s, Sunsokua underwent rapid [[Wikipedia:Economic_growth|economic growth]] and industrialisation, a period often referred to as the "[[Sunsokua Miracle]]". In the late 1730s and early 1740s, the country transitioned from a [[Wikipedia:One-party_state|one-party system]] under martial law to a [[Wikipedia:Multi-party_system|multi-party democracy]], with the first democratically elected High minister taking office in 1746.

Today, Sunsokua is a [[Wikipedia:Developed_country|developed country]] with an export-oriented economy, ranking [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|11th globally by nominal GDP]] and [[List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita|44th by GDP per capita]]. Major industries include oil, agriculture, and chemical manufacturing. The country is known for its strong economicfreedom, healthcare, and [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|human development indicators.]] Sunsokua is a [[Wikipedia:Semi-presidential_republic|semi-presidential republic]] with a [[Wikipedia:Bicameralism |bicameral legislature]], the National Legislature. It is regarded by some analysts as a [[Wikipedia:Great_power|great power]] and one of the most influential nations globally. While its [[constitution renounces the right to declare war]], Sunsokua maintains a robust [[Sunsokuan military|military]] for defence and peacekeeping purposes. The country is experiencing a significant population boom, driven by [[internal migration]] from the island’s south and from the [[Mahea|Mahean mainland]], as people seek economic opportunities. Sunsokuan culture is widely recognised internationally, particularly for its art, cuisine, and music, with parallels to neighbouring Ashain.
